subject: Next steps: dedicated capacity sizing call for NexaHealth
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@nexah.com>
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: scheduling dedicated capacity sizing call

Hi Sara — great to meet today, thanks for the walkthrough of NexaHealth's ingestion patterns and the demo goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goal: Book a 60-minute dedicated sizing + technical deep dive to capture throughput, P95 latency target, peak concurrency, and data residency constraints.
- Prep we need from your side: representative sample of request sizes (tokens per request or payload sizes), expected QPS/peak concurrency, and whether inference will be behind a batching gateway.
- Our team on the sizing call: me (sales), Priyom (solutions eng, will run the throughput/latency scenarios), and Grace (Customer Success for rollout & SLAs).

Suggested slots (PT):
- Wed Jun 2, 9:00–10:00 AM PT
- Thu Jun 3, 10:00–11:00 AM PT
- Fri Jun 4, 2:00–3:00 PM PT

I attached a brief workload template (nexah-workload-profile.xlsx) — filling that out ahead of the call will make the session far more actionable. Also attached a short proposed agenda (proposed-sizing-agenda.pdf). 

If you prefer, here's a one-click scheduler: https://cal.com/sergio/nexah-sizing-30min (I can extend to 60m on booking).

Thanks — happy to be flexible on timing.

Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0126
https://www.redwoodinference.com

From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@nexah.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Miller <t.miller@nexah.com>
Date: Tue, 29 May 2028 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: scheduling dedicated capacity sizing call

Thanks, Sergio — appreciate the concise recap. Tom (cc'd) is our platform lead and will want to validate the network/residency constraints. A few quick notes from our side:

- Target latency: 150ms P95 for the customer-facing endpoint (we know this is tight; likely needs small batch sizes).
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~45 rps; peak bursts could be up to ~220 rps during campaign windows.
- Payloads vary: 80% short prompts (~150 tokens), 20% long prompts (500–1,200 tokens).
- Data residency: EU-only for PHI-related data; some metadata can be processed in the US.

We can do Thu Jun 3, 10:00–11:00 AM PT. I also uploaded a CSV with anonymized sampling of request sizes to our shared drive (will share link after internal scrub).

Two questions for your team before the call:
1) Can Redwood run the sizing session in our preferred EU region (Frankfurt)?
2) Any initial guidance on whether quantized model variants would materially affect latency for 150ms P95?

I'll try to fill the attached workload template tonight.

—Sara
Sara Jones
Head of Platform | NexaHealth
